content: 1. Omeprazole increases the level or effect of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 enzymes. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. The effect of combining fedratinib with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors has not been studied. 2. Epinephrine (racemic) and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the erdafitinib dose in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ergoloid mesylates and ergotamine by reducing their metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. 5. Eribulin and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 6. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Clarithromycin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin and escitalopram both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of estradiol, conjugated estrogens, and estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose as tolerated. 15. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 17. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fesoterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Fexinidazole and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4 and may increase the level or effect of clarithromycin. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Fingolimod and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Fluvoxamine increases the level or effect of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Clarithromycin and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Fluphenazine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fluticasone (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, such as Cushing-type symptoms. 25. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of fluvastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, increasing the risk of myopathy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin increases the effects of fondaparinux by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of fosamprenavir and fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Combining futibatinib with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the risk of futibatinib toxicities. 31. Clarithromycin and gadobenate both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Clarithromycin and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. 34. Clarithromycin and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs during treatment and withhold therapy if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or changes by more than 60 ms from baseline. 35. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so monitor for increased risk of QTc prolongation if coadministration is unavoidable. 36. Clarithromycin and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Clarithromycin and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases the level or effect of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Clarithromycin increases the effects of heparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 43. Idelalisib increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 44. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Omeprazole decreases the level or effect of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Clarithromycin and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin and isradipine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Itraconazole increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole decreases the level or effect of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy.
